description: The Ormond Memorial Art Museum and Gardens presents an exhibition featuring different styles of portraiture from hyper-realism, to contemporary avant-garde, to modern classicism by three contemporary artists. Richard Currier’s hyper-realism evokes the humanity within the figures. Viewers are able to see beyond the highly realistic depictions to the person within. The avant-garde style in which Jeff Whipple creates his portraiture causes those who see his work to view the person through and in reference to the Spasm, a symbol comprised of three irregular lines and represents an individual life. Austrian born Robert Schöller’s process creates a modern classical style that harkens back to the great portrait painters such as Anthony Van Dyck and Gilbert Stuart. He was commissioned for a White House portrait due to his mastery of this style. These three distinguished artists combine to provide a new experience of portraiture.
title: "About Face"

description: This new vignette-adapted from a 1974 original that Jeannette Genius McKean (1909-89) installed at The Center Street Gallery in Winter Park- is planned around a mid-19th-century iron bed. The black bed, one of a pair from the museum's collection, is decorated with abalone shell flowers and birds and an intricate border pattern of both abalone shell and paint. This romantic room will also include a lithograph by Alphonse Mucha (1860-1939), paintings by both Jeannette and Hugh F. McKean (1908-95), a floral textile by Ava Maxwell, and a pair of Tiffany blown-glass candle lamps, c. 1905, that were a wedding gift to Jeannette's mother, Elizabeth Morse Genius (1872-1928). Mrs. McKean, the museum's founder and an accomplished artist and interior designer, created many vignettes for exhibit over the course of her career, and this particular installation pays homage to her love of this form of expression. These themed interior scenes developed from objects in the collection are now a fond tradition at the Morse and a unique and popular exhibit with visitors.
title: "The Now and Then Room"

description: The Story of Harness Racing by Currier & Ives, from the Harness Racing Museum & Hall of Fame in Goshen, N.Y., features rare original Currier & Ives lithographs, gear, and posters that tell the history of a mid-19th century American pastime that became a national sport. The lithographs in this exhibition depict great trotting horses, bucolic mid-19th century scenes, and comedic adventures that convey a picturesque view of Americana prior to the development of photography. Examine racing equipment, equine care tools, driver colors or uniforms, and other memorabilia up-close in the hands-on tack trunk. The History Center will complement the exhibition with a display of items from the Ben White Raceway that reflects the rich history of the horseracing industry in Central Florida. Included in general admission.
title: The Story of Harness Racing by Currier & Ives

description: As one of America`s Splendor Seekers, Otto C.Lightner "Collector of Collections" left behind an outstanding legacy in the form of a rare glimpse into the Gilded Age through art objects and artifacts with international flair relating to science and industry of the late 19th century. This exhibition explores and highlights some of his most exciting and historic purchases and includes: a rare Regency terrestrial globe; swan and Sphinx-decorated Egyptian revival furniture; oversized Oriental and European porcelains; Tiffany, Galle` and Brilliant-cut glass; animalistitic and portrait bronzes, selections from his treasury of silver and a variety of wall decorations, clocks and other richly ornamented objets d`art.
title: "The Weird and Wonderful: Unique Decorative Arts From the Lightner Museum, St. Augustine"
